title: no verb changes an issue's title, so a measurably false title is permanent -- and the issue that would record this cannot record it
body:
**NO VERB CHANGES AN ISSUE'S TITLE, SO A FILED TITLE IS PERMANENT EVEN WHEN IT IS MEASURABLY FALSE** -- and the issue that would naturally record this is itself unwritable for the same reason.

**MEASURED 2026-08-30 (vc), driven in a throwaway `intent init` under a fixture `$HOME`, never against the live register.**

```
intent issues            ->  add | show | close | open
intent issues add        ->  Usage: intent issues add [OPTIONS] <TITLE>
                             --severity  --body <text>  --from <file>
```

**`add` takes a TITLE and allocates the number itself. There is no id argument**, so an existing issue cannot be addressed by any verb that writes. `show` reads, `close` and `open` move status. **The register is CREATE-ONLY on both prose fields: title and body.**

**This is NOT reachable through `0131`'s upsert, and that was checked rather than assumed.** `0131` records `issues add` as a create implemented as an upsert, which sounds like an accidental update door. It is not one: the collision there is between two callers whose numbers were auto-allocated to the same value, and **a caller who wants to target an existing issue has no way to name it.** So no door exists, accidental or otherwise.

## The live case, and why it cannot be repaired

`0078` is titled `claude skills uninstall --force reports 'ok: 1 changed' at rc=0 while leaving the skill on disk and fully loadable`. **ic measured its `fully loadable` clause FALSE against this build** (2026-08-30, fixture `$HOME`): `uninstall` unlinks `SKILL.md` and leaves the DIRECTORY, so what survives is an unloadable husk. The issue's core claim -- rc=0, `1 changed`, something left on disk -- **still holds**, so the row must stay open; only its title is wrong.

**All three available responses are bad, which is the point of this filing rather than a complaint about `0078`:**

- **Close as superseded** -- retires a LIVE defect on the strength of a wrong title.
- **Leave it open** -- the register's triage surface carries a false claim indefinitely, and a title is what a reader triages on.
- **Refile** -- trades a wrong title for a DUPLICATE. Two numbers for one defect split its history and both decay independently, which is a Highlander violation inside the instrument the estate uses to track Highlander violations.

**RULED (vc, 2026-08-30): `0078` stays OPEN with its title known-wrong, and the correction is recorded at the reachable sites -- `0150`'s Related paragraph and ic's board -- rather than by minting a second number.** The general rule: **where a register has no edit door, a wrong title is corrected by ANNOTATION at a reachable site, never by a second number.**

## And the recursion is the finding, not a flourish

`0090` -- *issues add creates a body that no verb can write* -- is OPEN and **ITS OWN BODY IS EMPTY**, because no verb can write it. It is an instance of itself. **It therefore cannot be widened to cover the title half**, which is why that half needs its own number instead of an amendment, and why this issue exists as a separate row rather than as a paragraph in `0090`.

**Two prose fields, one defect class, and the register cannot describe its own gap in the row that names it.**

## What closes this

An `intent issues edit <NNNN>` door reaching title and body, subject to the same refusal discipline `0131` establishes for creates. **It is not enough for it to reach `body` alone**: `0090` names the body and `0078` is a title, and a fix that closed only the field already filed would leave the case that prompted the filing exactly where it is.
